idiom_name: interface/type alias document + JSON.parse, optional zod schema
implementation_notes: TypeScript types describe the document but are erased at runtime, so the realization is an interface (or a discriminated union) plus JSON.parse for decoding - and, at any trust boundary, a runtime schema (zod's z.object/parse/safeParse with z.infer) or hand-written guards that actually verify the document before it is used. That replaces the classic message class: types carry the contract for the compiler, the validator carries it for the running system, and the receiver switches on a discriminant field rather than on an operation name. exactOptionalPropertyTypes, readonly and branded types pin the contract harder, and unknown is the safe type for freshly parsed data until it has been narrowed. Byte-level parsing is only justified for fixed binary formats or streaming encoders.
pitfalls: Casting parsed JSON with 'as OrderShipped' is an unchecked assertion: the type exists only at compile time, so a document can be missing every field and still typecheck.
Structural typing makes any object with the same fields a valid document, so two message kinds with identical shapes are interchangeable unless a discriminant or a brand is added.
Excess-property checking applies only to object literals, not to parsed data, so producer typos surface at runtime or never.
Numbers follow JavaScript semantics (2^53 precision), so 64-bit identifiers must travel as strings and BigInt revival must be explicit.
